To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the measured fission fragment distribution in 238U + 12C is very sensitive to the excitation energy of the compound system.
the fission fragment distribution can provide a deep insight into the fusion-fission dynamics of a compound nucleus.
the isotopic fission-fragment distributions are very sensitive to the deformation path of the nucleus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the fission process in heavy systems, and its relation to fusion-fission.
nuclear structure effects in the fission process.
the study of fusion-fission reactions using the inverse-kinematics method, with the aim to obtain information on the fusion-fission dynamics, and the potential energy landscape in particular.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fission fragment distribution, as a function of the atomic number and the excitation energy, is an excellent probe to investigate the fusion-fission process, in particular to determine the potential energy landscape in a multidimensional deformation space.
the isotopic fission fragment yields are a very sensitive probe to the fusion-fission dynamics and the potential energy landscape.
, for the first time, a complete isotopic distribution of fission fragments has been measured for an asymmetric system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the experimental data are in good agreement with the predictions from the macroscopic-microscopic model of the potential energy, and with the predictions of a dynamical model of fission, based on the time dependent Hartree-Fock method.

we have been able to determine for the first time the isotopic yields in the fission of 250Cn, 248Cf and 246Bk, and we have been able also to identify the fission of the neutron-deficient isotopes 244Es and 242Md.
we have measured the isotopic distributions for a wide range of atomic numbers, and for the first time, we have been able to extract the potential energy surface for the fusion-fission reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isotopic fission-fragment distributions can be described by a simple model, which is based on a one-dimensional potential energy landscape.
the fission fragment distribution in the symmetric region is strongly dependent on the excitation energy, and that the isotopic distributions are very sensitive to the fusion-fission mechanism.
the isotopic distribution of the fission products is strongly dependent on the excitation energy.
